title: Euforia → Desespero: A Reversão Ainda Está em Dúvida?
author: Tight-Firefighter369

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
The trouble with marking euphoria and despair on a chart you already know the ending of is that the labels come out perfect every time. You find the top because you can see the top.

The version of this exercise that teaches you something is to cover the chart at the bar you are standing on and label only what is visible, then uncover one bar at a time. Much harder, and the only version that tells you anything about doing it live.

replies.author: Tight-Firefighter369
replies.body: That’s a fair point. I’m using those labels as part of market psychology, mainly to give the chart some directional context. “Euphoria” isn’t meant to predict the exact top or act as an entry signal. The actual decision comes from combining market psychology with technical analysis, news and other factors. I agree that testing it bar by bar in real time would be a better way to validate it.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: Bar by bar is where it shows up. When I tried it the right edge was the problem: the same candle read as euphoria or as a pause depending on what I already believed, and nothing on the chart settled it.
